answer: A stake-bonded reputation ledger makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a deposit of onyx-graded value before its claims count, and the bond only unlocks after a long horizon of honest work. An attacker who spawns a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand bonds, and one proven lie forfeits the whole deposit, pushing the fraudster off the ledge of profitability. Cheap identities stay worthless; only bonded history earns trust.
